summary: Secnidazole (Solosec) is a long-acting oral 5-nitroimidazole antimicrobial given as a single 2 g packet of granules. It is FDA-approved for bacterial vaginosis in female patients 12 years and older and for trichomoniasis in patients 12 years and older (treat sexual partners simultaneously). The granules are sprinkled on applesauce, yogurt or pudding and consumed within 30 minutes without chewing; it is not dissolved in liquid. It is generally well tolerated, the most common adverse effect being vulvovaginal candidiasis. It is contraindicated in nitroimidazole hypersensitivity and in Cockayne syndrome (risk of severe hepatotoxicity), and alcohol/propylene glycol should be avoided during and for 2 days after treatment.
indications: Bacterial vaginosis in female patients 12 years of age and older
Trichomoniasis (Trichomonas vaginalis) in patients 12 years of age and older - treat sexual partners simultaneously

Single 2 g packet of granules taken once

admin: Sprinkle the entire contents of the packet onto applesauce, yogurt or pudding and consume the whole mixture within 30 minutes without chewing or crunching the granules

moa: Secnidazole is a 5-nitroimidazole. After entering anaerobic bacteria and protozoa, its nitro group is reduced to reactive intermediates that damage microbial DNA, causing strand breakage and cell death. Its long elimination half-life provides sustained exposure from a single dose.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to secnidazole or other nitroimidazole derivatives
Cockayne syndrome (severe, sometimes fatal hepatotoxicity reported with structurally related metronidazole)
relative: Chronic/repeated use (avoid - rodent carcinogenicity with nitroimidazoles)
Concurrent alcohol or propylene glycol intake

preg: Limited data in pregnant women are insufficient to inform a drug-associated risk. Animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits showed no adverse developmental outcomes at up to ~4 times the clinical exposure. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed.
lact: Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment; discontinue breastfeeding for 96 hours after the single dose (based on the drug's long half-life). A lactating patient may pump and discard milk during this period.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is provided in the labeling; use with general caution.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is provided; contraindicated in Cockayne syndrome because of the risk of severe hepatotoxicity/acute liver failure seen with related nitroimidazoles.

moderate: Alcohol and preparations containing ethanol or propylene glycol - GI and disulfiram-like reactions (nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, dizziness, headache); avoid during and for 2 days after
minor: Combination oral contraceptives (ethinyl estradiol/norethindrone) - no clinically significant interaction; may be co-administered
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals; a high-fat meal does not significantly change exposure
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcoholic beverages and products containing ethanol or propylene glycol during therapy and for 2 days afterward
interactions.diagnostics: No clinically significant labeled laboratory test interference

serious: Severe hepatotoxicity (in Cockayne syndrome with related nitroimidazoles)
emergency: Signs of a severe allergic reaction (swelling, difficulty breathing, widespread rash)

monitoring: Development of vulvovaginal candidiasis (may need antifungal treatment)
For trichomoniasis, ensure partners are treated to prevent reinfection

pearls: Secnidazole IS FDA-approved (Solosec) - single 2 g oral granule dose for bacterial vaginosis and trichomoniasis (unlike some other agents in this set)
Sprinkle on soft food and swallow without chewing; do NOT dissolve in liquid
Avoid alcohol/propylene glycol during and for 2 days after (disulfiram-like reaction); contraindicated in Cockayne syndrome
For trichomoniasis, treat partners simultaneously and counsel STI prevention
missed: Secnidazole is a single-dose therapy, so a regular missed-dose schedule does not apply. If a patient vomits shortly after taking the dose or is unsure it was fully consumed, they should contact the prescriber rather than self-redose.
overdose: There is limited overdose experience. Symptomatic supportive care is recommended; nitroimidazoles in overdose may cause GI upset and neurologic symptoms. Contact a poison control center.
